headline: Fast-Paced Synonym Race Game for English Classes
problemStatement: Students learn new words, but in real speaking and writing they default to the same ‘safe’ choices. Synonym Showdown forces quick recall and shows the class better alternatives in seconds.
outcomes: Build lexical range by generating multiple alternatives for common words
Notice meaning differences (strong vs mild, formal vs casual) between near-synonyms
Increase speed: retrieve 3–10 alternatives under time pressure
Create better writing choices by expanding the word pool before a task
howItWorks: Choose a topic and difficulty; the game selects a target word that fits
Students type synonyms against the clock — points for valid answers
After the round, project the accepted words and quickly discuss which ones fit different contexts
Run a second round with a new word or the same theme to reinforce patterns
teacherUseCases: Pre-writing warm-up: expand options before a paragraph/essay
Unit review: synonyms for words from the week’s reading
Quick energy reset: 5–8 minutes of fast recall and discussion

faq.q: Do students have to find unique answers?
faq.a: No. If two students submit the same synonym, they both get credit. The goal is range and speed, not ‘gotcha’ uniqueness.

faq.q: How do I run this with a big class?
faq.a: Run one short round, then project the accepted word list and ask pairs to choose the best word for 2–3 example sentences (formal vs casual, strong vs neutral).

faq.q: Can I align it to my unit vocabulary?
faq.a: Yes. Set the topic to your unit theme (e.g., jobs, travel, environment). The target words will stay in that lane, so students practice synonyms they’ll actually use.
Yes with the easy setting. Start with high-frequency words where students can find 2–3 alternatives, then build up as confidence grows.

faq.q: Will it accept phrases or only single words?
faq.a: It depends on the prompt, but the goal is usable replacements. If a phrase is a realistic substitute, it can be accepted — and it’s a good teachable moment.

faq.q: Do students need to sign up?
faq.a: No. Students join with a link/code and submit from a browser on any phone or tablet.
